beats.text: Mad with grief for his son, Ravana rode out himself in his golden chariot, his ten heads crowned and his twenty arms armed.
He scattered the monkey army like dry leaves in a storm.
Rama had no chariot. So Indra sent his own divine chariot with its charioteer, Matali.
It came down from heaven, drawn by green horses, shining like the sun.
For days they fought, arrow against arrow. The gods watched from the sky.
Every time Rama cut off a head, another grew. A hundred heads fell, and a hundred grew back.
Then the sage Agastya appeared and taught Rama a sacred hymn to the sun, the Aditya Hridayam, to give him strength.
Rama could not defeat Ravana by ordinary means. Only one weapon remained.
